study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Lin et al., Journal of Affective Disorders, 2023
study_identification_part.si4_title: Understanding the heterogeneity of dynamic functional connectivity patterns in first-episode drug naïve depression using normative models

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract and introduction clearly state the goal to use normative modeling of dynamic fMRI features to quantify individual-level deviations in first-episode drug-naïve MDD and to assess heterogeneity and clinical relevance. This satisfies both stating research questions and the purpose of normative modeling.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text:
"This study combined the dynamic features of fMRI data and normative modeling to quantitative and individualized metrics for delineating the biological heterogeneity of FEDN-MDD." 
"we used the normative modeling approach that maps interindividual deviations... to understand the biological heterogeneity of MDD"

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study builds a new normative model using healthy controls from IBCDR with explicit eligibility criteria (age 18–50), image quality thresholds (head motion mean FD > 0.5 mm or max FD > 2 mm excluded), and provides final sample sizes and group allocations with reasons for exclusion (motion).
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "According to the information provided by IBCDR, we selected subjects... 1) FEDN-MDD aged from 18 to 50... 2) healthy controls with age in a range of 18 to 50... 3) subjects with excessive head motion (mean FD > 0.5 mm or max FD > 2 mm) were excluded, resulting in 274 FEDN-MDDs and 832 controls; 4) 125 healthy control individuals... (healthy-ICA)... 5) Another 289 healthy control individuals (healthy-base)... 6) 274 FEDN-MDD... and the rest 418 healthy control individuals (healthy-comparison)..."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Covariates age and sex are incorporated (sex-specific normative age models; regression includes sex and age). However, despite multi-site data, no explicit site-effect handling (e.g., site covariate, ComBat, hierarchical modeling) is described for the normative modeling step.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text:
"The data from the healthy-base group were used to construct the sex-specific normative age model." 
"the following quantile polynomial regression model was fitted... sex encodes the participant's sex... age is the modified age..."

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "We employed data from International Big-Data Center for Depression Research... (http://yanlab.psych.ac.cn/IBCDR). Full details on the datasets and preprocessing pipeline have been described previously (Yan et al., 2019)."

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing steps and QC criteria are described (discard first 10 volumes, slice timing, realignment, coregistration/segmentation, MNI normalization, bandpass 0.01–0.1 Hz; motion thresholds for exclusion). Software names/versions are not specified.

nm5_data_preprocessing.location: 1-s2.0-S0165032723001271-mmc1.docx.md: Methods – Data acquisition and preprocess (lines ~37–40); Lin2023.pdf.md: Dataset description (line ~81)

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: They applied 10-fold cross-validation on the healthy-base cohort to assess generalization, training on 90% and testing on 10%, yielding 10 normative models.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "To assess generalization, we applied 10-fold cross-validation... trained the polynomial regression model on 90% of the 289 healthy-base participants... withholding the remaining 10% for estimating generalization performance."

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The normative model trained on healthy-base was applied to an independent set of healthy individuals (healthy-comparison group) not used in model development.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "we next positioned each FEDN-MDD patient and healthy-comparison participant within the normative range for healthy-base adults of the same age and sex."

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: They specify the modeling approach as quantile polynomial regression (second-order), estimating 5th/50th/95th percentiles with bootstrapping, sex-specific, and using 10-fold CV. However, software/libraries and versions are not specified.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text:
"A quantile polynomial regression model was used to determine percentile curves based on the second-order polynomial regression..." 
"we specifically estimated the 5th, 50th (median), and 95th percentiles with bootstrapping confidence intervals..."

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: While cross-validation is described, no quantitative model fit or calibration metrics (e.g., explained variance, prediction error, coverage rates) are reported. The text notes most individuals fall within 95% CIs but provides no numeric assessment.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "most individuals were deemed to reside in the normative range with 95% confidence intervals"
